The blood work shows normal white blood cell counts and inflammatory markers, suggesting this is not a systemic infection or acute autoimmune flare. Have you noticed any fluid draining from the lesions, or do they form a cluster of blisters?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The cluster of similar lesions in your daycare and your brother's recent chickenpox are concerning for a viral etiology. Given the immunizations are up-to-date, have you noticed any vesicles (small fluid-filled blisters) forming on top of these papules, or are they solid bumps?

REQUEST TEST: IgM for Varicella-Zoster Virus
